union.summary: Blank-skipping in `Arguments.iterate` silently changes AND/OR/XOR semantics over cell ranges, and no test anywhere passes a range to those functions
union.evidence: The diff changes the shared `Arguments.iterate` (packages/sheets/src/formula/arguments.ts:110-125) to skip blank cells for *every* range, not just unbounded ones. `BoolArgs.iterate` is used by AND/OR/XOR (packages/sheets/src/formula/functions-logical.ts:111, 133, 174), so e.g. `=AND(A1:A3)` with A2 blank changes from FALSE (blank→false) to TRUE. Every AND/OR/XOR test in the suite uses literal arguments only (packages/sheets/test/formula/formula.test.ts:455-470, 1066-1067, 1325-1328); grepping the test tree for `AND(A`/`OR(A` over a range returns nothing. The new tests in this diff only exercise SUM/AVERAGE/COUNT, so the boolean-aggregation behavior change ships with zero coverage.

union.summary: All-blank / mostly-blank bounded ranges now change results for AVERAGE/MEDIAN/STDEV/VAR/GEOMEAN (e.g. AVERAGE → #VALUE!), with no test for those functions
union.evidence: With blanks skipped (arguments.ts:118-123), `averageFunc` reaches `count === 0` and returns `ErrNode.VALUE` (packages/sheets/src/formula/functions-statistical.ts:39-41) where it previously returned 0; `stdevFunc`/`varFunc` (639, 689) similarly flip to #VALUE! when fewer than two numeric cells survive. The only empty-data test added is `=SUM(A:A)` on an empty sheet → '0' (packages/sheets/test/sheet/calculation.test.ts:351-355). The repository has follow-up unit tests for MIN/MAX over blank ranges only (packages/sheets/test/formula/formula.test.ts:4412-4438) — nothing covers AVERAGE/MEDIAN/STDEV/VAR over an all-blank or single-numeric range, at either the formula or sheet level.

union.summary: YorkieStore changes (getUsedBounds + expandUnboundedRanges in all three buildDependantsMap branches, incl. batchOverlay) have no test
union.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:561-616 adds `ensureIndex()`/`bounds()` and rewrites formulas in the document branch, the batchOverlay-skip branch, and the overlay branch, plus a new `getUsedBounds()`. Grepping packages/frontend/tests for `A:A`, `SUM(A:`, `getUsedBounds`, or `expandUnbounded` returns no matches, and there is no yorkie-store unit test file covering buildDependantsMap. The MemStore equivalent is covered indirectly by test/sheet/calculation.test.ts, but the collaborative store path (where the overlay branches make the code non-trivial) is untested.

union.summary: New `CellIndex.bounds()` and `Store.getUsedBounds()` have no direct tests despite dedicated test files for both
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/store/cell-index.ts:128-149 adds `bounds()`. packages/sheets/test/store/cell-index.test.ts covers add/remove/clear/rebuild/size/cellsInRange/hasAnyInRange/getOccupied* but has no `bounds` case (file read in full, 201 lines). Likewise packages/sheets/test/store/store.test.ts contains no `getUsedBounds` assertion (grep for `getUsedBounds` matches only src files and docs). So the empty-index `undefined` result and the sparse min/max-across-independent-row/col-indexes behavior are only covered incidentally via sheet-level SUM assertions.

union.summary: New grammar alternatives `COL ':' REF` (`A:B1`) and `ROW ':' REF` (`1:B2`) are never lexed by any test; `$`-prefixed unbounded refs are never run through expansion
union.evidence: packages/sheets/antlr/Formula.g4 adds 7 REFRANGE alternatives, but the lexer-level tests only cover `A:A`, `1:1`, `B2:B`, `A:B`, `1:3` (packages/sheets/test/formula/formula.test.ts:4355-4370). `A:B2`/`$A:$A` appear only as plain strings passed to `isUnboundedRange`/`resolveRange` unit tests (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.test.ts:231-270), which bypass the regenerated ANTLR lexer entirely. A mistake in the regenerated FormulaLexer for the COL:REF / ROW:REF alternatives, or the fact that `resolveRange` strips `$` so `=SUM($A:$A)` expands to `=SUM(A1:A3)` (losing absolute markers), would not be caught.

union.summary: No test where an unbounded range includes the formula's own cell (self-reference / circular case)
union.evidence: Every sheet-level test parks the formula in column D while referencing column A or rows 1-3 (packages/sheets/test/sheet/calculation.test.ts:294-355), so the case that a whole-column/whole-row expansion swallows the formula cell itself (e.g. `=SUM(A:A)` in A5, or `=SUM(1:1)` in D1 where D1 is inside row 1) is never exercised. This is the classic pitfall of whole-column refs (circular reference / potential recalculation loop) and the diff ships no coverage for it.

union.summary: Documented limitation "cross-sheet unbounded refs evaluate to #ERROR!" is asserted only as a string passthrough, never evaluated
union.evidence: docs/design/sheets/formula.md (new "Limitations" paragraph) claims `Sheet2!A:A` evaluates to `#ERROR!`. The only test is `expect(expandUnboundedRanges('=SUM(Sheet2!A:A)', bounds)).toBe('=SUM(Sheet2!A:A)')` (packages/sheets/test/formula/formula.test.ts:4395-4399), which asserts the rewrite is skipped but not the claimed evaluation outcome. Grepping packages/sheets/test for cross-sheet unbounded refs (`Sheet2!A:A` in cross-sheet-calculation.test.ts) finds nothing, so the actual behavior (error vs. crash vs. silent wrong value) is unverified.

union.summary: Lowercase unbounded refs and the `try/catch` fallback path in expandUnboundedRanges are untested
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/formula/formula.ts (expandUnboundedRanges) calls `resolveRange(token.text.toUpperCase(), resolved)` inside a try/catch that falls back to the original text. No test passes a lowercase reference (`=sum(a:a)`, which would be rewritten to `=sum(A1:A3)`) and no test drives the catch branch, so both the case-normalization behavior and the failure fallback are uncovered.

union.summary: `Arguments.iterate` now skips blank cells inside *every* range (not just unbounded ones), changing the result of all existing bounded-range aggregations, but the diff adds no test for that change — and MIN/MAX over a range with no numeric cells is untested and regresses.
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/formula/arguments.ts (diff): `const isRange = isSrng(node.v); ... if (!cell || cell.v === undefined || cell.v === '') continue;` applies to any range, e.g. `=MIN(A1:A3)`/`=MAX(A1:A3)`/`=AVERAGE(A1:A3)` on a pre-existing bounded range. The only tests touching this are indirect (`=AVERAGE(B2:B)`→200, `=COUNT(A:B)`→5 in test/sheet/calculation.test.ts, and COUNT does not even use `iterate`). Searching the whole test suite for MIN/MAX over a grid range finds only literal-argument tests (test/formula/formula.test.ts:519-529). Consequently `minFunc`/`maxFunc` (src/formula/functions-statistical.ts:85-98, 110-123) leak their `Infinity`/`-Infinity` accumulator once blanks are skipped — the later main I could read contains exactly that fix plus new tests (`describe('Aggregations over ranges with no numeric cells')`, formula.test.ts:4412-4438) that are NOT in this diff, i.e. the regression shipped uncaught because this change has no direct test.

union.summary: The new range syntax now flows through formula-rewriting code paths that cannot parse it (row/column insert, delete, move, autofill), and no test covers a sheet containing `=SUM(A:A)` when structure changes.
union.evidence: `shiftFormula` (src/model/worksheet/shifting.ts:360-379) and `moveFormula` (ibid. 80-84) split a REFERENCE token on ':' and call `parseARef(endpoint)`; `parseARef` throws `Invalid Reference` for a column-only/row-only endpoint (src/model/core/coordinates.ts:362-369). The diff adds no test in test/sheet/shifting.test.ts, test/sheet/manipulation.test.ts, test/sheet/moving.test.ts or test/sheet/autofill.test.ts exercising insert/delete/move/fill on a sheet whose formula is `=SUM(A:A)` or `=SUM(1:1)`, so a throw/`#REF!` corruption on the newly-legal syntax would not be caught.

union.summary: New public `CellIndex.bounds()` has no unit test; it is only covered indirectly through MemStore calculation tests, so its own edge cases (data not starting at A1, becoming empty after removals, independent row/col minima) are unverified.
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/store/cell-index.ts:128-149 adds `bounds()`. packages/sheets/test/store/cell-index.test.ts (read in full, 201 lines) is untouched by the diff and contains no `bounds` reference — I grepped the whole test tree for `bounds` and got no hit in that file. E.g. `bounds()` returning `undefined` after `remove()` empties the index, or a sheet whose data starts at C5, is never asserted anywhere.

union.summary: The calculation test named "evaluates a whole-column reference on an otherwise empty sheet" does not exercise the `bounds === undefined` fallback it purports to cover — the formula cell itself is populated, so bounds is defined and the '0' assertion holds either way.
union.evidence: test/sheet/calculation.test.ts (diff): `const sheet = new Sheet(new MemStore()); await sheet.setData({r:1,c:4}, '=SUM(A:A)'); expect(...).toBe('0')`. Writing D1 populates the cell index, so `getUsedBounds()` returns `[{r:1,c:4},{r:1,c:4}]`, not `undefined`; the `bounds ?? [{r:1,c:1},{r:1,c:1}]` fallback in `expandUnboundedRanges` (src/formula/formula.ts) is never taken by this test. The undefined path is only covered by the unit test `expandUnboundedRanges('=SUM(A:A)', undefined)`.

union.summary: `expandUnboundedRanges` rebuilds the whole formula from tokens, but every rewriting test in the diff uses a single-function formula, so corruption of surrounding tokens (string literals, operators, whitespace, nested calls) would not be detected.
union.evidence: test/formula/formula.test.ts (diff) asserts only `=SUM(A:A)`, `=SUM(1:1)`, `=AVERAGE(B2:B)`, `=COUNT(A:B)`, `=SUM(1:3)`. The "leaves bounded formulas untouched" case returns via the `!tokens.some(shouldExpand)` fast path, so it does not test reconstruction at all. The later main I could read added exactly such a test (formula.test.ts:4379-4389), which is absent here.

union.summary: Two of the seven new grammar alternatives (`REF ':' ROW` and `ROW ':' REF`, i.e. `A1:2`, `1:B2`) are documented but untested at every layer.
union.evidence: antlr/Formula.g4 (diff) adds `REF ':' ROW | ROW ':' REF` and docs/design/sheets/formula.md documents `A1:2`, `1:B2`. But coordinates.test.ts only asserts `A:A, A:C, 1:1, 2:5, A1:B, B2:B, A:B2, $A:$A` for `isUnboundedRange` and `A:A, A:C, 1:1, 2:5, A1:B, B2:B, A:B2, A1:B2` for `resolveRange`; formula.test.ts and calculation.test.ts never use `A1:2` or `1:B2`. union.summary: The YorkieStore and ReadOnlyStore wire-in (`getUsedBounds`, plus three `expandUnboundedRanges` call sites in `buildDependantsMap` including both batch-overlay branches) has no test.
union.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts (diff) rewrites formulas in three separate loops and adds `getUsedBounds()` with a new `ensureIndex()` call; packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts adds `getUsedBounds()`. I searched packages/frontend for tests: the only file mentioning formulas over the Yorkie store is tests/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-cross-sheet.integration.ts (not a `*.test.ts`, so not part of the unit run) and it uses only bounded refs. No test asserts a whole-column dependants entry or recalculation via YorkieStore, nor whole-column evaluation in a read-only sheet.

union.summary: Two behaviors the PR explicitly documents are asserted nowhere: a cross-sheet unbounded ref evaluating to `#ERROR!`, and `extractFormulaRanges` tolerating (skipping) unbounded refs for highlighting.
union.evidence: docs/design/sheets/formula.md (diff) states `Sheet2!A:A` "evaluate to `#ERROR!`" and "Whole-column/row highlighting (`extractFormulaRanges`) skips unbounded refs". union.summary: Error/fallback branches of the new coordinate helpers are untested: `parsePartialRef`'s throw, `expandUnboundedRanges`' try/catch fall-through, and `$`-marked endpoints in `resolveRange`.

union.summary: No test for a self-referential whole-column/row formula (e.g. `=SUM(A:A)` written into column A), which the new syntax makes trivially reachable and which interacts with circular-reference detection.

union.summary: `resolveRange` test names claim clamping that the assertions disprove for explicitly-given endpoints beyond the bounds.

per_sample.summary: Error/fallback branches of the new coordinate helpers are untested: `parsePartialRef`'s throw, `expandUnboundedRanges`' try/catch fall-through, and `$`-marked endpoints in `resolveRange`.
per_sample.evidence: src/model/core/coordinates.ts (diff) `parsePartialRef` throws `Invalid Reference` when an endpoint has neither column nor row, and `expandUnboundedRanges` (src/formula/formula.ts) has a `catch { /* fall through to the original text */ }` branch. No test in coordinates.test.ts or formula.test.ts drives either path, so the fallback could be dead or wrong. Likewise `isUnboundedRange('$A:$A')` is asserted but `resolveRange('$A:$A', bounds)` / `resolveRange('$B$2:$B', bounds)` are not.

per_sample.summary: No test for a self-referential whole-column/row formula (e.g. `=SUM(A:A)` written into column A), which the new syntax makes trivially reachable and which interacts with circular-reference detection.
per_sample.evidence: All new calculation tests place the formula in column D (`{r:N,c:4}`) so the expanded range never contains the formula cell. With bounds derived from the used extent (which includes the formula cell), `=SUM(A:A)` in A5 expands to a range covering A5 itself; no test in test/sheet/calculation.test.ts asserts the resulting behavior (`#REF!`/cycle detection vs. silent wrong value).

per_sample.summary: `resolveRange` test names claim clamping that the assertions disprove for explicitly-given endpoints beyond the bounds.
per_sample.evidence: src/model/core/coordinates.test.ts (diff): `it('clamps a whole column to the data extent')` asserts `resolveRange('A:C', bounds)` = `r(1,1,3,3)` with maxC=2, and `it('clamps a whole row ...')` asserts `resolveRange('2:5', bounds)` = `r(2,1,5,2)` with maxR=3 — i.e. the explicit endpoints are not clamped. The assertions are meaningful, only the test names mislead about the contract.
